title: Serverless LLM Architecture
summary: Separate request admission from elastic inference capacity so serverless execution can scale safely despite model startup and duration constraints.
overview: Serverless LLM architecture delegates capacity provisioning to a platform while the application supplies request handling, model execution, or orchestration. It may use managed inference, GPU containers, functions that call hosted models, or asynchronous workers. Serverless does not imply that a large model fits a short-lived general-purpose function or starts instantly.

The core architecture decouples interactive deadlines from elastic startup. A gateway can serve warm capacity for interactive work and place delay-tolerant tasks in a durable queue. State, idempotency, and artifacts remain external to ephemeral workers. Platform-specific concurrency, duration, accelerator, and scaling limits must be verified before committing to the design.

production.poc: A prototype measures both warm and cold behavior and confirms the platform can run the intended model or API orchestration.
production.production: Production uses durable queues, external state, bounded concurrency, and clear synchronous versus asynchronous contracts.
production.scale: Enterprise scale manages regional quotas, startup storms, cost visibility, and minimum capacity for workloads that cannot tolerate scale-from-zero delay.

components.name: Request gateway
components.role: Authenticates requests and selects synchronous or asynchronous handling.

components.name: Durable queue
components.role: Buffers accepted delayed work with stable task identifiers.

components.name: Elastic inference workers
components.role: Load approved artifacts and execute within platform resource limits.

components.name: External state store
components.role: Persists task status, results, and idempotency records.

components.name: Autoscaling controller
components.role: Adjusts capacity using backlog, concurrency, and startup lead time.

flow.title: Classify latency needs
flow.description: Decide whether the task requires immediate response or can return a job identifier.

flow.title: Accept work durably
flow.description: Persist task identity and enqueue before acknowledging asynchronous acceptance.

flow.title: Scale compatible capacity
flow.description: Request workers with the required accelerator, memory, and runtime support.

flow.title: Initialize and execute
flow.description: Wait for real readiness, then run the task under deadline and resource limits.

flow.title: Persist the result
flow.description: Commit validated output and completion before acknowledging queue delivery.

flow.title: Scale down safely
flow.description: Drain active work and rely on external state for later retries or status queries.

useCase.title: Processing periodic inspection reports
useCase.situation: A property platform summarizes inspection documents uploaded in bursts after site visits.
useCase.problem: Keeping peak GPU capacity running continuously is expensive, but reports can tolerate queued processing.
useCase.requirement: Scale processing with demand while preserving every accepted report and its status.
useCase.architecture: Uploads create durable jobs consumed by elastic inference workers; results remain in external storage.
runtime: The user receives a job identifier after durable acceptance.
A worker starts, loads the approved model, processes the report, and commits the result.
useCase.failure: If the worker exceeds its execution limit, the queue retries the same task identity and avoids duplicate accepted results.
useCase.impact: Measure job completion age, cold-start contribution, cost per accepted report, and retry volume; low idle cost must be weighed against delayed availability.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds cold-start delay and capacity uncertainty.
Requires job status and delayed-result interfaces.
Reduces the economic benefit of zero idle workers.

failures.detection: Backlog rises while worker count stops increasing.
failures.recovery: Apply admission limits and expose realistic deferred status.

failures.detection: The queue redelivers an apparently unfinished task.
failures.recovery: Use stable IDs and transactional completion records.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming serverless means stateless business logic
mistakes.fix: Persist task progress and results externally.
Measure the full time to useful capacity.
Bound backlog according to retention and completion objectives.

whenToUse: Use for bursty delay-tolerant inference jobs.
Use when platform-managed capacity fits the model requirements.
Use for lightweight orchestration around hosted inference.
whenNotToUse: Avoid scale-to-zero for strict low-latency workloads without warm capacity.
Do not assume accelerator availability in every platform tier.
Avoid long tasks that exceed supported execution limits.
checklist: Verify platform resource and duration limits.
Track cost and completion age together.
